subject: Data retention exception - post-call follow up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <dpo@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T15:10:00Z
Subject: Data retention exception - post-call follow up

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Goal: support Acme’s conversational product while meeting your PII and data retention requirements (including your ask for no persistent content storage for sensitive sessions).
- Items we promised to follow up on:
  1) Clarify what Redwood can and can’t remove (content vs. operational logs vs. embeddings).
  2) Proposed mechanics for a data-retention exception (scope, timeframe, and audit controls).
  3) Sample exception wording and an internal review path.

High-level answers: Redwood can support session-level zero-content retention for specific routes by disabling content persistence and KV-cache dumping for that route, while retaining minimal operational telemetry for debugging and billing. However, we typically keep short-lived transaction logs for 7 days (redacted) to support availability/resiliency and incident response.

Requested next steps: can you confirm the exact scope (which API routes/endpoints and which user types) where you need 0-retention? I’ll loop in security and legal to draft an exception we can send to you.

Attaching: initial summary of our logging controls; I’ll send a draft exception after an internal review.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <dpo@acme.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Data retention exception - post-call follow up

Camila — thanks for the quick recap. We have two main asks that we need Redwood to address before we move forward:

1) 0-retention for conversation content for any calls that contain PII (we can define PII fields). No content should be persisted to disk or long-term storage after the response is returned.
2) Minimized logging: we can accept ephemeral transaction IDs and success/failure codes for 72 hours only. No request/response payloads, no embeddings, and no KV cache dumps containing PII can be retained.

Questions for Redwood:
- Do you store embeddings derived from content by default? If so, can embedding storage be disabled per-customer or per-route?
- If you retain minimal operational logs for 7 days as you mentioned, can those be redacted (no payloads) and limited to non-identifying metadata (timestamp, request id, model id, region)?
- Is there an option to terminate any backups/snapshots that might include data in case of a legal hold?

We can sign an exception if Redwood provides clear definition and controls. Please loop in security and legal.

—Alex
Data Protection Officer, Acme Corp
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T10:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Data retention exception - post-call follow up

Team — forwarding Alex’s reply. Key asks: 0-retention for PII-containing sessions, embeddings disabled per-customer/route, and logs limited to 72 hours (redacted). They’ve said they can sign an exception.

Can security/legal confirm:
- Feasibility of per-customer or per-route zero-content retention (runtime flag to avoid persisting to object store and to prevent embeddings from being created/stored).
- If we need to change our default 7-day operational log retention to 72 hours for this account, impact on debugging/incident response and whether we can provide alternative controls (e.g., on-call playbook with additional tracing for incidents within an agreed SLA window).
- Wording for a limited-scope data-retention exception we can send to Acme that covers: definition of PII, exact retention windows, what logs remain, encryption/KMS controls, and process for emergency data access (legal hold).

I’m happy to coordinate the review and a quick sync with Acme if helpful.

Thanks,
Camila
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data retention exception - post-call follow up

Camila/Marissa/Rafael — I reviewed and drafted a narrow exception that should be acceptable to Acme. High-level:

- Scope: Apply to production API routes specified by Acme (we’ll insert route list once confirmed).
- Content retention: Redwood will not persist conversation content, embeddings, or KV cache exports for scoped routes. Ephemeral in-memory processing still occurs to serve requests.
- Operational logs: Redwood will retain redacted transaction metadata (timestamp, request_id, model_id, region, success/failure code) for 72 hours. No payloads, embeddings, or PII fields will be stored in logs for this account.
- Backups/snapshots: We will exclude scoped account data from standard backup snapshots; for disaster recovery we’ll provide an agreed playbook and will only restore data with explicit written approval.
- Audit: We’ll include monthly access reports and quarterly SOC2-related evidence on controls.

I’ve attached a draft PDF and a short summary of logging controls. Rafael — please review the technical feasibility for disabling embeddings per-route and excluding routes from snapshots. Marissa — can you confirm commercial implications (any impact to pricing or SLOs)? I’ll refine the draft and we can send to Acme for signature (DocuSign link to follow).

—Neha
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <dpo@acme.com>, Acme API Team <infra@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T14:05:00Z
Subject: Proposed data-retention exception and next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear requirements. Attached is our proposed exception and a short controls summary (see attachments). Main points: 

- Scope: Scoped routes (please confirm route ids) will have 0-content retention: no conversation content, no embeddings stored, and no KV-cache exports persisted. In-memory processing is performed to serve the request, but nothing is written to long-term storage.
- Operational logs: Redacted transaction metadata retained for 72 hours (timestamp, request_id, model_id, region, error codes). No request/response payloads or PII in logs.
- Backups: Scoped account data excluded from standard backups; any restore requires explicit written approval from Acme legal/ticket.
- Emergency access/legal hold: We will follow a documented process; legal hold requests will be evaluated and require coordination with Acme legal and Redwood senior leadership.
- SLO impact: There may be a small increase in incident-response ramp time without 7-day payload logs; we’ve committed an on-call playbook and can provide additional tracing for incidents affecting this account. Commercial: Marissa, Rafael — can you confirm whether there’s a commercial adjustment for this exception?

If this looks good I’ll open a DocuSign envelope and send the exception for signature. Let me know any edits and confirm the route list to scope.

Next steps:
- Acme: confirm route ids and approve draft exception
- Redwood: internal sign-off (security & legal) and DocuSign envelope

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- data-retention-exception-draft.pdf (draft exception; signature-ready after our final edits)
- redwood-logging-controls-summary.pdf (one-pager on what we retain and redaction controls)
